pages.name: A rule gives a slope
pages.text: A hot part sits in a 20 °C room. It cools at a tenth of its gap, in °C a minute. The rule is `dT/dt = −0.1 × (T − 20)`. `dT/dt` is the slope: how fast the temperature `T` changes with time `t`. Like `dv/dt` in `i = C dv/dt`, it is a rate. A rule that ties a rate to the thing itself, or to time, is a [[differential equation]]. At 80 °C the gap is 60 °C, so the part falls at 6 °C a minute.

pages.name: What −6 means
pages.task: At 80 °C the rule gives −6 °C a minute. What does that number tell you?
pages.answer: How fast it is falling now
pages.why: `dT/dt` is a rate at one moment, like a speed. At 80 °C the part is falling at 6 °C a minute. As it cools, the gap shrinks, so the rate shrinks too. In all it falls nearly 60 °C, towards the room.

options: How fast it is falling now
How far it falls in all

pages.name: Arrows everywhere
pages.text: The rule gives a slope at every time and temperature. Draw each as a short arrow and you get a [[slope field]]. The slope depends only on the gap, so arrows at one height match. At 50 °C the slope is −3 °C a minute. At 20 °C it is 0. At 10 °C it is +1, so below the room the arrows point up. Its only rate is `dT/dt`, so it is [[first order]]. Filled in, they tip steeply down when hot and flatten near the room.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. room 20 degrees. Every row of arrows is filled in.

pages.name: The arrow at 35 °C
pages.task: The probe sits at 35 °C, in the 20 °C room. What slope does the rule give there, in °C a minute?
pages.why: The gap is 35 − 20 = 15 °C. The rule takes a tenth of it with a minus sign: `−0.1 × 15 = −1.5`. So the part falls at 1.5 °C a minute, and the arrow tips gently down.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room 20 degrees. gap 15 degrees. gap to the room: 35 minus 20 equals 15 degrees. slope: minus 0.1 times 15 equals minus 1.5 degrees a minute.

pages.name: Follow the arrows
pages.text: A curve that follows the arrows everywhere is a [[solution]]. From 80 °C it falls steeply, then levels off towards the room. It is the cooling curve you met with exponentials. It levels off because the gap shrinks, and the rate shrinks with it. Starts at 50 °C and 10 °C give other curves under the same arrows. So the rule fixes the slopes, and a start picks one curve. Every curve heads for the room line.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room. Curves start at 80, 50 and 10 °C. Each follows the arrows and levels off towards 20 °C.

pages.name: Number or curve
pages.task: The part starts at 80 °C. What is the solution of its rule?
pages.why: A solution gives the temperature at every moment, so it is a whole curve. 20 °C is only where it heads. −6 °C a minute is only its slope at the start.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room. its temperature at every moment.

pages.name: The steady state
pages.text: At 20 °C the gap is zero, so the rate is zero. The flat line `T = 20` has a slope of zero all along it, just as the rule asks. So it is a solution too, called a [[steady state]]. A part that starts at room temperature stays there. This rule is Newton's law of cooling. It is a simple model that holds best for a modest gap. Whatever the room's temperature, its flat line is a steady state, and every curve heads for it.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. steady state T equals 20 degrees. The room is at 20 °C. Curves from 80, 50 and 10 °C all head for its flat line.

pages.name: A 30 °C room
pages.task: Now the room is at 30 °C. Which is the steady state?
pages.why: In a 30 °C room the gap is zero at 30 °C, so the rule asks for no change there. The flat line at 30 °C has a slope of zero everywhere. So it is a solution, a whole curve that never changes.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 30). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. steady state T equals 30 degrees.

pages.name: Try a curve
pages.text: To check a candidate curve, compare its slope with the rule's at every point. Try a straight line from 80 °C, falling 6 °C a minute. It matches at the start. At 50 °C it still falls 6, but the rule wants 3. At 20 °C it still falls 6, but the rule wants 0. Wherever the two disagree, the line is marked as a mistake. No straight line from 80 °C can follow the arrows, because the rule's slope changes with the gap.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room 20 degrees. matches at 80 degrees. line minus 6, rule minus 3. line minus 6, rule 0.

pages.name: Is it a solution?
pages.task: The straight line starts at 80 °C and falls 6 °C a minute. Is it a solution of the cooling rule?
pages.why: A solution must match the rule's slope everywhere. The line matches only at 80 °C. At 50 °C it falls 6 °C a minute while the rule wants 3. So it is not a solution.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room 20 degrees. line minus 6, rule minus 3. line minus 6, rule 0.

pages.name: A rule in time
pages.text: A rule can depend on time instead. In `dy/dt = 2t`, the slope of `y` is twice the time `t`. So every arrow in one column matches. The arrows are flat all down `t = 0`, yet no flat line solves it. At `t = 2` the rule wants a slope of 4. The parabolas `y = t² + c` follow every arrow, because the slope of `t² + c` is `2t`. A start picks `c`, as when you integrated.
pages.alt: Rule: d y by d t equals 2t. y up the side, time t along the bottom. Arrows show the slope 2t: flat at t = 0, tipping up for later times and down for earlier ones. flat at t equals 0. slope 4 at t equals 2. y equals t squared plus c. Parabolas y = t² + c follow the arrows.

pages.name: Which curve solves it?
pages.why: The slope of `t² + 4` is `2t` at every `t`, so it follows every arrow. `y = 2t` has a slope of 2 everywhere, and the flat `y = 3` has a slope of 0. Each matches the rule at one time only.
pages.alt: Rule: d y by d t equals 2t. y up the side, time t along the bottom. Arrows show the slope 2t: flat at t = 0, tipping up for later times and down for earlier ones. y equals t squared plus 4.

pages.name: A cold part
pages.task: A part at 15 °C sits in the 20 °C room. Which way does its temperature go?
pages.why: The gap is 15 − 20 = −5 °C. The rule gives `−0.1 × (−5) = +0.5`, so the part warms at 0.5 °C a minute. Its curve rises and levels off towards the room line.
pages.alt: Rule: d T by d t equals minus 0.1 times (T minus 20). Temperature T in degrees up the side, time t in minutes along the bottom. Arrows show the rule's slope at each point: steep down when the part is hot, flat at the room, pointing up below it. room. gap to the room: 15 minus 20 equals minus 5 degrees. slope: minus 0.1 times ( minus 5) equals plus 0.5 degrees a minute.
